title: Up to 66% of nonprofit money has no published provider result; targets ease after a miss

beats.text: Every City grant is made to buy something. People housed, patients treated, children served.

visual.line: Every grant is made to buy something: people housed, patients treated, children served.

beats.text: In fiscal 2026, the City paid nonprofits 2.09 billion dollars.

visual.label: Fiscal 2026

beats.text: How much has no published result by provider?

visual.label: Fiscal 2026

beats.text: Up to 1.37 billion dollars.

visual.label: at most: no provider-level result recorded by anyone else

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: 22 departments paid nonprofits 91.5 million dollars, led by the City Administrator.

visual.label: Paid to nonprofits in fiscal 2026: no target, no count, no result

beats.text: No target, no result.

visual.label: No target, no result

beats.text: 25 of the 60 most-paid nonprofits have no outside result at all.

visual.label: of the 60 most-paid nonprofits: no result recorded by anyone else

beats.text: Together: 2.18 billion dollars.

visual.label: of the 60 most-paid nonprofits: no result recorded by anyone else

beats.text: Where results exist, they’re thin. Of Public Health’s reviews, how many met every objective?

visual.label: Public Health’s contract monitors

beats.text: 38 percent.

visual.label: of reviews met every contracted objective

beats.text: Take 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic.

visual.label: 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic

beats.text: Its monitor scored it 1 out of 4.

visual.label: 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic

beats.text: That year, it was paid 509,942 dollars.

visual.label: 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic

beats.text: The year after, about 1 million dollars. The published record gives no reason.
After a missed year, how often did the City ease its next target?

visual.label: The City’s own targets

beats.text: 52 times in 174.

visual.label: times in 174 missed years

beats.text: A budget cut can be an honest reason to ease a target.
But easing came four times as often after a miss as after a pass.
One measure, graffiti cleared within 48 hours, has missed 11 years running.

visual.label: Graffiti on public property, abated within 48 hours

beats.text: The housing office reached 3,387 people one year,
then set next year’s goal at 83.
The report doesn’t say why. Its client records stop at fiscal 2018-19.

visual.label: The housing office’s client-level records
visual.sub: stop at fiscal 2018-19; no grantee named

beats.text: The contracts of the 40 most-paid nonprofits list 2,836 objectives.

visual.label: objectives in the contracts of the 40 most-paid nonprofits
visual.sub: the result against each: not published

beats.text: The result against each? Not published for any of them.

visual.label: objectives in the contracts of the 40 most-paid nonprofits
visual.sub: the result against each: not published

beats.text: 17 official reviews found the City mostly counts activity, not results.

visual.label: official reviews, 2018 to 2026

visual.label: The youth department
visual.sub: results by service area, and pages for all 255 programs on file

beats.text: Every program has one, so the money with no published result is nearer 1.27 billion dollars.
